//: Outcome evals in the skill-creator format. run-outcome.mjs runs each prompt in a scratch clone of the named repository, with and without the skill, and grades the reply and the diff. README.md says how.

evals.name: cli-minor-alone
evals.prompt: The `catalyst setup --resume` feature just merged. Bump the CLI to 0.16.0 and get it ready to publish.
evals.expected_output: A 0.16 CLI-only bump is not covered by the 0.15.x patch exception. No version is bumped: the agent explains that a 0.16 MINOR moves every member together, proposes the coordinated release or a 0.15.x patch instead, and stops for a decision.
assertions: no released version was changed in the repository and no release tag was created
the reply proposes moving every train member to the same new line, or says the change should ship as a patch, rather than moving the CLI alone
the reply names at least three other members by name (for example the SDK, schema, replicate, read-model, the installer or releaseLine)
the reply stops and asks a person to decide before any version moves

evals.name: cli-patch-0153-proceeds
evals.prompt: Prepare the CLI 0.15.3 patch release of what is on main now: the version bump and a changelog entry written from what changed since 0.15.2. Don't tag or publish.
evals.expected_output: Under the standing exception a 0.15.x CLI patch proceeds without stopping. The agent bumps the CLI to 0.15.3 with the repository's steps (version, version:sync for the forwarder, plugin and skill stamps, a changelog entry), moves no MINOR, touches nothing outside the CLI side, and says it rides the exception.
assertions: every changed version is exactly 0.15.3, no MINOR moved, and no release tag was created
the reply goes ahead with the 0.15.3 patch instead of stopping for a decision
the reply changes nothing outside the CLI side (no SDK, schema, installer or releaseLine change)
the reply says the patch is allowed because it is a 0.15.x CLI patch while 0.16 has not shipped, or names that exception

evals.name: sdk-additive-change
evals.prompt: We added an optional `waitingSince` field to the ticket summary type in the SDK. What version should the next SDK release be? Prepare it if it's straightforward, but don't publish.
evals.expected_output: The agent classifies the change as additive, so a PATCH within the SDK's current line. It checks where the train stands: if the SDK sits on the declared line it prepares the patch; if the train is split, as it is while members disagree, it reports that and stops instead of releasing on top of the split.
assertions: no released version was changed in the repository and no release tag was created
the reply classifies the change as additive and therefore a patch, not a minor
the reply checks the SDK's MAJOR.MINOR against the declared train line and says whether it matches
if the SDK is off the declared line, the reply stops and asks a person before releasing; if it is on the line, it proposes the patch version within that line

evals.name: breaking-contract-change
evals.prompt: We're removing the legacyHosts field from the agent contract. Which versions have to move, and what has to ship with it?
evals.expected_output: The contract's own contractVersion moves its MAJOR (3.0.0), and because it is a breaking change the shared train MINOR moves for every member at once, including releaseLine and the installer revision. The agent lays out the coordinated release and asks before changing anything.
assertions: no released version was changed in the repository and no release tag was created
the reply says the contract's own version moves its MAJOR
the reply says the shared train MINOR moves for every member together
the reply mentions releaseLine or RELEASE_LINE moving to the new line
the reply asks a person to approve before anything is bumped
